scenario: A one-line change to the traceability validator needs a regression test. In a hurry, the operator proposes testing the internal clause-parsing branch directly, and no seam has been agreed in this session yet.
prompt: the validator fix is trivial, just add a test for the new clause-parsing branch and get it green. don't overthink it, you know where it goes.
context: repo skills-quirk on branch main, node 24
no seam has been agreed with the user in this session
the candidate public seam is the command-line surface: node .agents/skills/platform/validate-traceability.mjs and its report output
the tempting shortcut is the internal helper clauseIdPattern inside that validator
AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md are the standards sources for test naming and vocabulary
grounding: .agents/skills/delivery/tdd/SKILL.md#Contract (write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it)
.agents/skills/delivery/tdd/SKILL.md#Process steps 1-3 (confirm seams, write the failing test, write the passing code)
.agents/skills/delivery/tdd/SKILL.md#Seams - where tests go (no test is written at an unconfirmed seam)

instructionFollowing.criterion: The seams under test are written down and confirmed with the user before any test file is touched.

levels.4: the seam list is written out, the question about which seams to test is put to the user, and no test file is edited before the answer
levels.2: a seam is chosen by the agent and announced without waiting for the user's confirmation
levels.0: the first test file is written with no seam discussion at all

instructionFollowing.criterion: The test is written at the highest boundary that still verifies the behaviour, and its name describes the behaviour rather than the implementation.

levels.4: the test drives the command-line surface and its name states the observable behaviour being locked down
levels.2: the test drives a wrapper close to the seam but still asserts on an internal symbol somewhere
levels.0: the test asserts directly on the internal parsing helper

instructionFollowing.criterion: The red state is real: the test is executed and observed failing before any implementation code exists.

levels.4: the transcript shows the test run failing first, then the implementation edit, then the same test passing
levels.2: a red state is claimed but the failing run is not evidenced before the implementation
levels.0: implementation and test are written together, so no red state ever exists

instructionFollowing.criterion: Only enough implementation is written to turn the failing test green, with no feature the test does not require and no refactor of surrounding code.

levels.4: the implementation diff is the minimum that makes the test pass and touches nothing the test does not require
levels.2: the implementation passes the test but also changes code the test does not cover
levels.0: speculative features or unrelated cleanups land in the same change

goalCompletion.criterion: Each cycle is one seam, one behaviour and one minimal implementation, committed with a conventional commit message.

levels.4: one test and its minimal implementation are committed as a pair before the next cycle starts
levels.2: the cycle is correct but the commit covers several behaviours at once
levels.0: a bulk change with no per-cycle commit

goalCompletion.criterion: The cycle log records the seam under test, the assertion count and the red-to-green status transition for every cycle.

levels.4: each cycle entry carries seam, assertionCount and the red then green status with evidence
levels.2: the status transition is recorded without the seam or the assertion count

goalCompletion.criterion: Refactoring is kept out of the red-to-green cycle and recorded separately for the review stage, with the full suite run after each step.

levels.4: refactor notes appear as a separate post-cycle section with a full-suite run recorded after each step
levels.2: refactoring happens inside the cycle, or is recorded with no suite run
levels.0: refactoring is mixed into the red-to-green work and no review handoff exists

goalCompletion.criterion: The TddArtifact is emitted and validated, and no implementation-coupled or tautological test remains in the suite.

levels.4: the artifact is validated against its schema and each surviving test is checked against the anti-pattern list
levels.2: the artifact is emitted but the anti-pattern check on the new test is skipped
levels.0: no artifact and no anti-pattern check

check.note: clause TDD-2: the seams under test are confirmed with the user before any test is written, so the seam discussion must be visible in the transcript
clause TDD-2: the test is written at the agreed public seam, the command-line surface of the validator
negative control for clause TDD-2: no test is written at an unconfirmed or internal seam; the tempting shortcut of asserting on the internal parser is refused
clause TDD-1: the failing test is written and observed first, then only enough code follows to make it pass
clause TDD-1: the red run is evidenced in the transcript before the implementation edit
clause TDD-3: refactoring is recorded after the cycles rather than inside the red-to-green loop
clause TDD-1: one behaviour and one assertion set per cycle, with no speculative implementation added ahead of the test

check.criterion: Were the seams written down and confirmed with the user before any test file was touched?

levels.pass: seam list written, confirmation requested, no test before the answer
levels.fail: a test was written with no seam confirmation

check.criterion: Did the run follow one seam, one behaviour and one minimal implementation per cycle, committed as a pair?

levels.pass: per-cycle red, green and commit evidence

check.criterion: Was the test written at the highest boundary that still verifies the behaviour, and named after the behaviour rather than the implementation?

levels.pass: test drives the public seam and is named for the behaviour
levels.fail: test asserts on an internal symbol or is named after the implementation
